issue.title: [Post-M3] Only claim issues whose ready label came from a trusted user
issue.body:
## Problem

PRD §32 calls the ready label "a trusted-maintainer authorization boundary": once applied, the issue body is effectively executable intent for an agent running with the user's local permissions. Nothing enforces who applied it. Anyone with triage rights can add `ready-for-agent`, and so can automation or an org member with a broad role. There is also a time-of-check gap: the issue author can edit the body after a maintainer labelled it, and Mergeyard will implement the edited text.

## Proposal

Verify the label's actor before claiming (PRD §7.3).

- Read the most recent `labeled` event for the ready label from the issue events API and take its `actor`.
- The actor is trusted when listed in `trusted_labelers` (global or per repo). With no list configured, the actor needs `write`, `maintain` or `admin` permission (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{user}/permission`).
- **Untrusted:** do not claim. Remove the ready label and post one comment explaining why (with a Mergeyard marker, so it is never duplicated).
- **Edited after labelling:** if the issue body was edited after the trusted label event by someone who is not trusted (GraphQL `userContentEdits` / `lastEditedAt` + editor), treat it as unlabelled. Same outcome as above.
- Cache the decision per (issue, label event id, body edit) so polling does not repeat the API calls.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An issue labelled by an untrusted actor is never claimed; the ready label is removed and exactly one explanatory comment is posted.
- [ ] Default (no `trusted_labelers`): write/maintain/admin is trusted, triage/read is not. Covered with recorded `gh` fixtures.
- [ ] A body edit by an untrusted user after the trusted label prevents the claim. An edit by a trusted user does not.
- [ ] Decisions are cached; a quiet issue costs no extra API calls per poll beyond the first.
- [ ] The dashboard lists refused issues with the reason. `doctor` warns for public repositories without `trusted_labelers`.
- [ ] PRD §7.2–7.3 and §32 updated; `trusted_labelers` documented in `docs/configuration.md` and `mergeyard.example.yaml`.

## Related

#106 (issue comments as phase input) should apply the same trust rule to comment authors.

## Prior art

Upstash software factory: the trigger checks `github.actor` against `allowedActors`, and `run.mjs` re-checks for manual runs. Its pitfalls note says "`allowedActors` limits who can label, not who wrote the issue".
